transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (AtlasPay - Head of AI), Priya Menon (Infra Lead), Ethan Cole (Security), Sasha Rivera (Product)

Auto-generated summary: Quick alignment on POC scope, performance targets, and security gates.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jordan: Jordan here.
[00:10] Priya: Priya on infra.
[00:12] Ethan: Ethan, security.
[00:14] Sasha: Sasha, product.
[00:16] Maya: Maya from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Samir: Cool. So objective today is to scope the POC - figure out success criteria, what to benchmark, and decide which deployment mode makes sense: Hosted, Dedicated, or Private.

[00:35] Jordan: High level context - AtlasPay is rolling out an intelligent payments assistant for merchant support. Two main workloads: conversational agent for support (chat) and embeddings-based reranking for transaction lookup. We care about latency (customer-facing) and strict data controls for transaction data.

[01:05] Samir: Great. Can you give ballpark numbers - qps, avg tokens per request, and peak concurrency?
[01:12] Jordan: For chat we're seeing about 8 rps average across regions, peaks up to ~60 concurrent sessions during batch hours. Avg tokens per message ~200, but context windows can reach 2k with history. Embeddings: batch jobs ~10k docs/day, and realtime lookup queries maybe 20 qps, small tokens.

[01:40] Maya: Okay makes sense. For the POC we typically ask for a 24-48 hour traffic trace and representative prompt set so we can reproduce latency and cost profiles. We'll also run a throughput benchmark with synthetic concurrency.

[02:00] Priya: Our infra constraints: we must use VPC peering for any Dedicated or Private options, egress locked down, and some customers require EU data residency. Also, cost center prefers not to overprovision GPUs for alpha.

[02:25] Ethan: Security: SOC2 is table stakes, we need audit logs, SSO (SAML/Okta), and KMS-backed key management for any private keys. For Hosted, we need contractual assurances and controls around redaction/auditability.

[02:45] Samir: Totally. Quick mapping: Hosted: fastest to get started, Redwood-managed, can support region residency for data at rest in many cases; Dedicated: reserved capacity (GPU pools) for predictable throughput and isolation; Private: VPC/on-prem for fully customer-managed networking and KMS integration. Each has tradeoffs on latency, cost, and operational overhead.

[03:15] Sasha: For success criteria, product is mainly focused on: 95th percentile latency < 250 ms for short replies, tail under 500 ms for long context, and embedding recall within our existing baseline (we have an eval set). Cost target is roughly equal or less than current managed provider - we don't have exact numbers yet but we want unit cost down by 20% if possible.

[03:50] Maya: Noted. For the POC we propose measurable KPIs: (1) Latency: p50/p95/p99 across requests; (2) Throughput: sustained qps with concurrency; (3) Cost: estimated tokens per million and effective $/1M tokens; (4) Quality: run your eval set for embeddings and chat quality checks (we can ingest evals).

[04:20] Jordan: That sounds good. Question on caching and batching - how much does that impact latency? Our concern is customer-facing chat, so we can't add lots of batching.

[04:32] Maya: Right. Redwood's runtime supports workload-aware batching and prefix/KV caching; for chat we keep batching minimal to preserve latency, but prefix caching is helpful for repeated prompts and system messages. We can show results with batching off and with conservative batching to compare cost/latency tradeoffs.

[04:50] Priya: On Dedicated vs Hosted - if we go Dedicated, what's the typical lead time and what network setup is needed?

[04:58] Samir: Dedicated lead time is typically 1-2 weeks for provisioning in most regions once contract is signed; network setup needs VPC peering and some egress rules. For Private/on-prem it's longer — deployment window depends on their environment, usually 2-6 weeks with infra assistance. Hosted can be immediate for a small pilot.

[05:25] Ethan: For KMS integration, do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in Hosted or only in Private?

[05:32] Maya: We support CMK for Dedicated and Private more directly. For Hosted we have options depending on tenancy—some enterprise customers use a dedicated instance with envelope encryption and customer-controlled KMS; we'll include specifics in the security pack.

[05:50] Jordan: Benchmark plan and timeline?

[05:55] Maya: Proposed POC timeline (4 weeks):
Week 0 (onboarding): env access, traffic dump, prompt sets, baseline measurements.
Week 1 (benchmarks): run throughput and latency benchmarks across Hosted and Dedicated config variants; run embeddings eval against your test set.
Week 2 (tuning): quantization/precision and batching adjustments, measure cost delta.
Week 3 (user-quality eval): run product-level QA, compare to baseline, finalize SLOs.
Decision at end of week 4 with a recommendation. We can compress to 2-3 weeks if AtlasPay provides traffic and infra quickly.

[06:45] Sasha: For evaluation, we want a pass/fail checklist: latency, error rate < 0.1%, embeddings MRR improvement over baseline, and operational checklist (SSO, audit logs, KMS).

[07:00] Samir: We'll produce a POC report with dashboards: per-route latency, token-level costs, trace logs, and a summary recommendation. We'll also share our model catalog options and quantization profiles to hit cost targets.

[07:20] Priya: Any gotchas with GDPR / EU data residency? We have EU tenants and need data at rest in EU and limited egress.

[07:27] Maya: We can pin data residency in Hosted for many regions, Dedicated definitely supports region pinning, and Private obviously is customer-controlled. We'll include the residency options in the pack + contract language suggestions.

[07:42] Ethan: On monitoring - do you expose token-level cost breakdowns and tracing? We need to tie requests back to audit logs for compliance.

[07:49] Samir: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and trace hooks. We'll enable audit log export to your SIEM and can integrate with your SSO.

[08:05] Jordan: On the model side - are you using open models or proprietary ones? Licensing is a concern for us.

[08:12] Maya: We support curated open models and partner-verified models. For production we recommend models validated on your evals; licensing differs by model and we'll call out options. If you need higher throughput we can recommend quantized checkpoint variants.

[08:30] Priya: For Dedicated - what are scaling options? We don't want to pay for idle GPUs outside of peaks.

[08:36] Maya: Dedicated has autoscaling policies with reserved baseline and burst capacity. You can set autoscale rules by latency SLOs or by CPU/GPU utilization. That gives cost predictability while handling peaks.

[08:55] Sasha: Quick question - how do fallbacks work if a model fails or capacity is constrained?

[09:01] Samir: Smart routing lets us fallback to compatible model variants or to a lower-cost tier to avoid outages. We also support canary rollouts and A/B tests for new model versions.

[09:18] Jordan: Sounds good. For the POC we want comparisons: Hosted baseline (quick to stand up), Dedicated with reserved capacity for peak loads, and Private only if Hosted/Dedicated fail security gates. Is that fair?

[09:28] Samir: Yes, that's a common pattern — quick pilot on Hosted, then Dedicated if you need capacity/SLA and isolation, and Private if regulatory or KMS needs force it.

[09:40] Maya: Action items recap - we'll share benchmark harness, you share traces and evals, we run tests and reconvene.

[09:50] Ethan: One last thing - SAML integration and SCIM for provisioning?

[09:55] Samir: Yes, we support SAML/Okta and SCIM for user provisioning; we'll include the integration steps.

[10:05] Sasha: Great. Thanks everyone.
[10:08] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with the pack and scheduling.

End of transcript.
